svg.title: Tangent rigidity isolates the bounded affine-Springer point
svg.desc: Inside the open arc orbit of the reduced Schubert bound, the Springer condition is a closed finite-jet condition. A tangent is a nonzero-weight Laurent principal part X. The regular invertible adjoint matrix forces X regular, so its class is zero. The Noetherian determinant argument gives an open reduced point. The exact SL3 example has six root-jet coefficients, with adjoint block three one zero three and six-by-six determinant 729. A torus nilpotent Laurent direction persists in the full Grassmannian outside the bound.
svg.text: The central Levi point is isolated in its Springer bound
Characteristic zero • arbitrary connected reductive G • AS.1–AS.6
1. A finite-type orbit neighborhood, with all coefficient tests
A(u) ∈ m[[u]], M = C_G(λ), g₀ = u^λ; ad(A₀)|n invertible
Z = Spr_(G,A) ∩ closure(O_λ); O_λ = L⁺G · u^λ
The orbit is open in the reduced Schubert bound.
[X] ∈ T_g₀ O_λ: X is a finite principal part in n((u)).
Closed Springer tangent equation: [A(u),X] ∈ n[[u]]
D(u) = ad(A(u))|n has a regular inverse ⇒ X ∈ n[[u]]
AS.2–AS.5 • the zero-weight and torus orbit tangents vanish in the quotient
2. Six exact SL₃ root-jet coefficients
C = diag(1,1,−2) + E₁₂; λ(u) = diag(u,u,u⁻²)
Positive weight three: E₁₃ and E₂₃, each at u⁻¹, u⁻², u⁻³
u⁻¹
(a₁, b₁)
u⁻²
(a₂, b₂)
u⁻³
(a₃, b₃)
[C,X]: (aⱼ,bⱼ) ↦ (3aⱼ + bⱼ, 3bⱼ)
Regularity kills each pair: bⱼ = 0, then aⱼ = 0.
Family A(u) = diag(1,1,−2) + (1 + uϑ)E₁₂:
3bⱼ = 0, 3aⱼ + bⱼ + ϑbⱼ₊₁ = 0; b₄ = 0; det = 729
Exercises 3.S and 3.U • 3 and 9 are units over every coefficient k-algebra
3. Zero tangent gives an open point
q is the maximal ideal of the local ring.
T_g₀ Z = 0 ⇒ q/q² = 0
Finite generators: v = Cv, Cᵢⱼ ∈ q
det(I − C) is a unit ⇒ q = 0
A finite-type affine neighborhood
has B_f = k: an open reduced point.
Also for −λ and its opposite bound.
AS.6 and the local determinant proof
4. The full torus functor is larger
G = Gₘ; R = k[ε]/(ε²)
Bound at uᵐ: one reduced point
Full Springer: all of Gr_(Gₘ)
uᵐ(1 + ε/u) is a valid loop.
Its quotient factor is not an arc.
This nilpotent direction is outside Z.
Exercise 3.T • full nilpotents retained
Global cotangent: §§3.27–3.29. Satake support and proper-pushforward survival remain required.
